title: Pulse-arrival-time modulation did not establish improved ECG–PPG respiratory-rate fusion across two clinical datasets
abstract: Adding ECG-to-PPG peak-arrival-time modulation to fixed five-modulation respiratory-rate fusion did not establish reduced error: BIDMC gain -0.251 breaths/min (95% CI -0.528 to 0.020); independent CapnoBase gain 0.003 (-0.156 to 0.161). A label-free fixed algorithm was evaluated on 50 of 53 intensive-care and all 42 independent perioperative records with eligible windows. Baseline fusion included PPG intensity, amplitude and interval plus ECG amplitude and interval. Paired record-level bootstrap intervals and window, frequency-band, lag and annotation checks did not support consistent improvement. This limits this timing surrogate and fusion rule, not all respiratory information in pulse arrival time.
